question: Flu vaccines are reformulated every year. Why has measles vaccine, grown from a 1954 virus sample, never needed updating?
options: Its RNA copies itself with few errors
Its surface proteins cannot change and still work
It targets proteins hidden inside the virus
answer: Its surface proteins cannot change and still work. Measles mutates like other RNA viruses, but a 2015 study found that changes to the sites antibodies bind on its H protein mostly broke its grip on the receptors it needs to enter cells. A strain from a Boston schoolboy still covers every genotype.
move: When something never changes, ask whether it can afford to.
trap: Assuming a vaccine that never ages means a virus that never mutates.
reference: Fulton et al., Mutational analysis of measles virus suggests constraints on antigenic variation of the glycoproteins, Cell Reports, 2015
